niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why You Always Pick the Middle Option
ideas.angle: This video exposes the Decoy Effect, showing how companies deliberately introduce a useless third option to trick your brain into buying the most expensive item. It surprises viewers by revealing that their purchasing choices are heavily manipulated by simple spatial framing.

hook.en: You are being tricked into spending more.

ideas.reason: Behavioral economics and pricing tricks are performing exceptionally well on Shorts right now because viewers instantly relate to making purchases and feeling manipulated.
sources: Behavioral Economics studies on asymmetric dominance

ideas.title: Why Everyone Is Not Staring At You
ideas.angle: This video explains the Spotlight Effect, proving that people remember your embarrassing moments a fraction as much as you think they do. It provides immediate relief and taps into universal social anxiety.

hook.en: Nobody noticed your most embarrassing moment.

ideas.reason: Self-improvement and social anxiety shorts consistently drive high retention and comment engagement as viewers reflect on their own insecurities.
sources: Cornell University Spotlight Effect Studies by Thomas Gilovich

ideas.title: Make Someone Like You By Asking This
ideas.angle: This video breaks down the Benjamin Franklin Effect, demonstrating the counterintuitive truth that asking someone for a small favor actually makes them like you more, rather than annoying them.

hook.en: Want them to like you? Ask this.

ideas.reason: Actionable social psychology hacks that alter interpersonal relationships have viral potential because viewers immediately want to test them in real life.
sources: Studies on cognitive dissonance in social behavior
